Calculation method formulas and coefficients used

Water‑glycol mixtures · Melinder (2010)

Density, specific heat and freezing point are calculated with the Melinder polynomials, Properties of Secondary Working Fluids for Indirect Systems (IIR, 2010), using the coefficients published in the CoolProp library:

f(x, T) = Σi=0..3 Σj=0..5 cij · (T − Tm)i · (x − xm)j

T is the temperature in K, x the glycol mass fraction (0–0.6). ρ is in kg/m³, cp in J/kg·K. The freezing point uses only row i = 0 and is in K. Valid range: from the freezing point to 100 °C.

Pure water

Density according to Kell (1975), t in °C:

ρ = (999.83952 + 16.945176·t − 7.9870401·10⁻³·t² − 46.170461·10⁻⁶·t³ + 105.56302·10⁻⁹·t⁴ − 280.54253·10⁻¹²·t⁵) / (1 + 16.879850·10⁻³·t)

Specific heat: 7th‑degree polynomial fitted to IAPWS‑95 values at 101.325 kPa between 0 and 100 °C, with u = t/100:

cp = Σk=0..7 ak · uk  [kJ/kg·K]

Deviation from IAPWS‑95: less than 0.015 kg/m³ in density and less than 0.0001 kJ/kg·K in specific heat.

Ethylene glycol · coefficients cij

Propylene glycol · coefficients cij

Heat duty. Q = ṁ · cp · (T₂ − T₁). With a volume flow, ṁ = V̇ · ρ, with ρ and cp at the chosen evaluation temperature. When a temperature is calculated, the properties depend on the result, so the calculation is repeated until the value stops changing (fixed-point iteration). 1 kW = 859.845 kcal/h.

Note. At concentrations close to 0 % the Melinder polynomial deviates by about 0.1 % from pure water (for example 997.3 versus 998.2 kg/m³ at 20 °C). For water without glycol, choose “Water”.

Calculation method formulas used

Moist air · ASHRAE Handbook Fundamentals (2017), ch. 1

Water vapour saturation pressure according to Hyland and Wexler, T in K, pvs in Pa. Above 0 °C (over water):

ln pvs = −5800.2206/T + 1.3914993 − 0.048640239·T + 4.1764768·10⁻⁵·T² − 1.4452093·10⁻⁸·T³ + 6.5459673·ln T

Below 0 °C (over ice):

ln pvs = −5674.5359/T + 6.3925247 − 9.677843·10⁻³·T + 6.2215701·10⁻⁷·T² + 2.0747825·10⁻⁹·T³ − 9.484024·10⁻¹³·T⁴ + 4.1635019·ln T

Derived quantities (t in °C, p in kPa):

x = 0.621945 · pv / (p − pv)    φ = pv / pvs(t)
h = 1.006·t + x·(2501 + 1.86·t)  [kJ/kg d.a.]
v = 0.287042 · (t + 273.15) · (1 + 1.607858·x) / p  [m³/kg d.a.]
ρ = (1 + x) / v

Wet bulb and dew point

Thermodynamic wet bulb t* (adiabatic saturation), with xs* the saturation humidity ratio at temperature t*. For t* ≥ 0 °C:

x = [(2501 − 2.326·t*)·xs* − 1.006·(t − t*)] / (2501 + 1.86·t − 4.186·t*)

For t* < 0 °C:

x = [(2830 − 0.24·t*)·xs* − 1.006·(t − t*)] / (2830 + 1.86·t − 2.1·t*)

The wet bulb is found by solving the equation by bisection. The dew point is the temperature at which pvs = pv; below 0 °C it is the frost point. Pressure from altitude Z: p = 101.325·(1 − 2.25577·10⁻⁵·Z)5.2559 kPa. Specific heat: cp = 1.006 + 1.86·x kJ/(kg d.a.·K).

Calculation method sources, tables and accuracy

Equations of state · CoolProp 8.0

Properties come from the reference Helmholtz‑energy equations of state, evaluated with CoolProp 8.0 (HEOS backend). The blends R410A, R407C, R404A, R454B and R513A use the multi‑fluid model with the ASHRAE 34 nominal composition and the binary parameters of Lemmon (2004) for the HFC pairs, Bell (2022) for R1234yf/R134a and Bell (2023) for R32/R1234yf. Bubble and dew curves of the blends are traced with CoolProp's phase‑envelope routine.

These calculations were used to generate tables embedded in the page, so it also works offline:

saturation: ~200 log‑spaced pressures, from psat(Tmin) to 0.99·pc
vapour and liquid: 48 pressures × 26 / 22 columns in w = √u
uvap = (T − Tdew)/(Tmax − Tdew)   uliq = (Tbub − T)/(Tbub − Tmin)
R744 supercritical: 44 pressures (pc–150 bar) × 148 temperatures

Between nodes, 4‑point cubic Lagrange polynomials are used in log p and in w (density as ln ρ). The grids follow the saturation curve, so they never cross the two‑phase dome. Pressure at a given temperature is obtained by inverting the saturation curve with Newton’s method.

Conventions and accuracy

Reference state. For all fluids h = 200 kJ/kg and s = 1 kJ/kg·K for saturated liquid (bubble point) at 0 °C, the IIR convention. Some manufacturer tables for R717 and R744 use a different reference: enthalpy differences are unaffected.

Zeotropic blends. At the same pressure, saturated liquid is at the bubble temperature and saturated vapour at the dew temperature. Glide is Tdew − Tbub. Superheat is measured from the dew point, subcooling from the bubble point. For a given quality, h, s and v are the weighted mean of the saturated phases. The temperature is estimated by linear interpolation between bubble and dew (≈).

Accuracy versus CoolProp (820 test points below 0.9·pc): Tsat < 0.001 K, psat < 0.001 %, h < 0.06 kJ/kg, ρ < 0.03 %, cp < 0.4 %. Between 0.9 and 0.99·pc: h < 0.25 kJ/kg, cp up to a few % near the critical point. R744 supercritical: h < 0.6 kJ/kg, cp up to 3 % along the pseudocritical line.

Gauge pressure is relative to 1.01325 bar. 1 psi = 0.0689476 bar.

GWP₁₀₀ according to IPCC AR4. Safety class per ISO 817 / ASHRAE 34. For blends, Tc and pc are the maximum‑pressure point of the computed phase envelope.
